messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered: smart-routing fallback loop detected for customer-facing chat endpoints in eu-west. Severity: P1. Alerting on-call. Symptoms: repeated routing between model-variant 'redwood-model-a-fp16' and 'redwood-model-a-quant', increased 5xx and tool_call failures.

jess: seeing the alert, joining. can someone confirm impact window and which customers? :eyes:

simon: i'm oncall. I'm pulling traces now. 5xx spike started at ~1759993280, peaked ~1759993480. Affected route: /v1/chat/stream (hosted). Error signature: "tool_call unsupported on variant: redwood-model-a-quant" and occasional OOM on region failover.

infra-oncall: grabbing routing logs. early sign: smart-route policy is configured to prefer eu-west-1 fp16, fallback order includes quant variants in eu-west and then us-east. There's an edge where quant variant advertises support for tool_call in metadata but actually rejects calls at runtime.

ml-runtime: fwiw from runtime traces: quantized binary (redwood-model-a-quant) compiled without TOOL_CALL shim; calls hit a 422 with payload: `{\n  \"error\": \"tool_call_not_supported\",\n  \"variant\": \"redwood-model-a-quant\"\n}`. The router interprets that as transient and retries, which triggers failover to fp16 in same region, but due to concurrent retries it flips back -> loop.

sara: customer-impact summary from CS: two enterprise customers in eu-west observed intermittent failures during checkout flows using assistant tool integration. Estimated affected requests ~2.1% of total chat traffic in that region for the 10m window. No data loss reported but UX failures causing support tickets.

kevin: can we hotfix by changing fallback order to prefer us-east fp16 as second hop and reduce retries?

simon: proposing immediate mitigation: 1) update smart-routing policy to remove redwood-model-a-quant from eu-west fallback pool, 2) reduce route retries from 3 -> 1 for chat routes, 3) pin active variant to fp16 for flagged customers. I'll apply 1 & 2 now.

ml-runtime: +1 on removing quant from fallback. Also pushing a quick telemetry filter to prevent treats of TOOL_CALL errors as transient.

infra-oncall: applying policy patch: `PATCH /routing/policy/smart-route-1` payload: ```
{
  "fallback_order": ["redwood-model-a-fp16-eu-west-1", "redwood-model-b-fp16-us-east-1"],
  "max_retries": 1
}
```

pagerduty-bot: simon acknowledged the P1 at 1759993345. Escalation: pager duty rule triggered to ENG-SRE.

simon: policy patch applied at 1759993392. rolling out to all routers. watching metrics.

jess: note: i've DM'd the SEs for the two customers and told them we're mitigating and will update in 15m.

ml-runtime: observed latency/backoff behavior normalizing. error rate dropped from 3.8% -> 0.4% over 2 minutes. no more tool_call_unsupported errors on live traces.

sara: CS notified customers at 1759993510. Customers acknowledged — they're keeping session logs for postmortem.

kevin: we should also block the quant variant from being advertised as tool_call compatible in model catalog. that seems like the root cause (metadata mismatch).

ml-runtime: agreed. filing quick follow-up: MODEL-CATALOG-2662 to remove tool_call capability flag from redwood-model-a-quant until we validate. Also starting a regression job to confirm compiled artifacts include tool_call shim.

infra-oncall: creating a short-lived metric dashboard: `routing.loop.detect` and `tool_call.unsupported` correlated with `routing.retries`. will keep it for 72h retention.

simon: handing off to day-shift oncall @sara in 20m for monitoring and follow-ups. if anything flares, please @simon and escalate to eng-sre.

jess: wanted note for postmortem: 1) incorrect capability metadata in model catalog 2) router retry semantics treat capability errors as transient -> flip loop 3) lack of safety check when toggling fallback pools.

ml-runtime: quick repro snippet for devs (from traces):
```
# client request -> router -> variant
POST /v1/chat
{ "model": "redwood-model-a", "tool_call": {"name":"lookup"} }
# router attempts redwood-model-a-quant -> returns 422 tool_call_not_supported
# router treats 422 as transient, retries -> hits redwood-model-a-fp16 -> success
# concurrent retry interleaving causes router to re-evaluate and flip back to quant
```

kevin: is there any risk that other quant variants are similarly mis-declared? we should run a quick audit across catalog.

ml-runtime: starting catalog audit now. will post results in #eng-ml when done. initial quick scan: 3 variants flagged for manual review.

sara: CS asked for ETA on permanent fix for customers. Recommended: full fix in 48-72h (catalog cleanup + router classification change). Communicated that to customers at 1759993640.

pagerduty-bot: incident P1 acknowledged by simon -> status: mitigated (policy patch applied). monitoring mode.

jess: adding action items: ACTION-1: run model catalog audit and revoke tool_call capability for miscompiled variants (owner: ml-runtime). ACTION-2: router: change policy semantics to treat capability errors as non-transient by default (owner: infra-oncall). ACTION-3: add e2e test that exercises tool_call end-to-end for all variants pre-publish (owner: eng-ml).

simon: leaving note: will join postmortem meeting at 1600 UTC. handing active watch to sara.

sara: accepted handoff at 1759993910. will continue monitoring and coordinate postmortem writeup. :white_check_mark:

cs-bot: CS ticket created: CS-48221 for the two affected customers, linked to incident P1-1759993333.

jess: thanks everyone. small follow-up: please include sample traces + router decision logs in the postmortem.

---
(automated) timeline summary: incident opened 1759993333, mitigation patch applied 1759993392, customer notif 1759993510, handoff complete 1759993910.
